title: Lists in depth: one list or two

terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the boarding list here, and try your classes from main.

tasks.title: Copy the booked list, and add a late name
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1`, write a class `Boarding` with a method `static List<String> withLate(List<String> booked, String late)`. It gives back a new list: everyone booked, in order, then `late` at the end, unless `late` is booked already. The caller can add to the list it gives back. `booked` stays as it is, and it may be a list made with `List.of`.

Check hands `withLate` lists of its own, some made with `List.of` and one empty, with names it makes separately, as names read in would be. It reads the list that comes back, adds a name to it as a caller may, and reads the caller's list afterwards to see it has not changed.
nextSteps: Read the parts of the lesson about List against ArrayList, and about a list that never changes.
Write the first line of the method with the types the task gives.
Make a new list of your own from booked.
Add late to it only when it is not on it yet, and give it back.
hints: booked may be a list that can never change, so the method never changes it. Everything it changes is a list it made itself.
A new list made with another list in its brackets is a copy that can grow. A name typed in is another String object, so look for it with a method that compares with equals.
Inside: `List<String> boarding = new ArrayList<>(booked);`, then `if (!boarding.contains(late)) { boarding.add(late); }`, then `return boarding;`.

tasks.title: Free a seat by its number
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a class `Seats` with a method `static int free(List<Integer> taken, int seat)`. It takes the seat numbered `seat` off `taken`, the caller's own list, and gives back the position the seat was at. When the seat is not taken it changes nothing and gives back -1. A seat is on the list once at most.

Check calls `free` with lists of its own, one with a seat whose number is also a position on the list, one with a seat numbered past the end of the list, one with a seat above 127, one empty, and reads both what `free` gives back and the caller's list afterwards.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about remove taking a position or a value.
Find the seat's position first, with the method that gives back -1 when it is not there.
When it is there, take it off the caller's list.
Give back the position you found.
hints: On a list of Integer, the same method name takes off an item by position or by value, and Java picks by the type you hand it.
Once you know the position, take the item off by that position: on a list of Integer, a plain int means a position.
Inside: `int at = taken.indexOf(seat);`, then `if (at >= 0) { taken.remove(at); }`, then `return at;`.

tasks.title: Void tickets while walking the list
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a class `Tickets` with a method `static int voidAll(List<Integer> sold, List<Integer> voided)`. It takes every ticket number in `voided` off `sold`, the caller's own list, keeps the others in their order, and gives back how many it took off. `voided` stays as it is.

Check calls `voidAll` with ticket numbers of its own, all above 127 and each made separately: two tickets next to each other, the last two, the last one, every ticket, none, and nothing sold at all. It reads what comes back, `sold` afterwards, and `voided` to see it has not changed.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about changing a list while you walk it.
For each ticket, ask voided whether it holds that number.
Take the ticket off with the iterator, count it, and give back the count.
hints: A for-each loop over sold cannot take items off sold. Walking positions forward skips the item after each one taken off.
An iterator can take off the item it just gave you, and keeps its place right. Asking voided whether it holds a number compares with equals, not ==.
The loop: `Iterator<Integer> it = sold.iterator(); while (it.hasNext()) { if (voided.contains(it.next())) { it.remove(); count++; } }`.
